title: “AI should be for finance, not for fine art.”  For one night only, in...
transcript: If you are wondering why Jessica Vosk, Billy Porter and Billy Zane are starring in essentially a 60 minute musical ad for ramp, well let me fill you in. This is a throwback to the old industrial musicals when companies would put together full scale musicals about their products, from toilets to bathtubs, These musicals have largely been lost to time since they were really only performed for shareholders and employees at these companies. But some cast recordings and videos do exist. And they were absolutely wild. And while they have since fallen out of favor, Bill Pay the musical is bringing that back for one night only. And let me tell you, they spared no expense with this thing. Not only was there an open bar and free snacks, but the actual production itself was surprisingly extravagant with many physical set pieces and tons of costumes. And while the prospect of sitting through a 60 minute ad doesn't sound all that appealing, the show was incredibly self aware, constantly making fun of itself, and filled to the brim with musical theatre references from wicked to Hairspray. And while if I'm being honest, I still can't really tell you what ramp does. I did have a really great time. I mean, how could you not love a show with a Kill Bill inspired fight sequence, Billy Zane doing a Fosse inspired dance number, Tap dancing hobbits, and Kevin from the office for some reason. The whole thing was just a very Loving tribute to this forgotten art form
